hypotheses.text: Anterior temporal pole T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is consistently absent in individuals with biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 mutations across all pediatric and adolescent stages, with white matter pathology restricted to periatrial and periventricular regions.
hypotheses.rationale: Deep testing revealed contested claims regarding temporal lobe involvement in biallelic NOTCH3 cases. While classic adult CADASIL and biallelic cysteine-altering variants show anterior temporal pole hyperintensities, multiple cohorts of biallelic loss-of-function (frameshift, nonsense, null) variants specifically report anterior temporal pole sparing alongside periventricular or periatrial leukomalacia-like volume loss.

evidence.text: In three patients from two unrelated families with homozygous NOTCH3 frameshift variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 presenting at 9 to 14 months of age with vascular leukoencephalopathy, MRI showed extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes, and calcifications, but the anterior temporal lobes were explicitly spared.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants across 26 patients lead to a distinct neurodevelopmental disorder with periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, clearly segregated from biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) that present with adult-onset CADASIL-spectrum deep white matter lesions.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype

hypotheses.text: The spatial distribution of white matter changes in recessive NOTCH3 disease differentiates loss-of-function mutations from cysteine-involving missense mutations by showing periatrial/periventricular volume loss in the former and confluent anterior temporal pole hyperintensities in the latter.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolving whether the radiological dichotomy between LoF and cysteine-altering variants is binary requires evaluating whether periventricular volume loss vs anterior temporal hyperintensity provides complete separation on neuroimaging across cohorts.

evidence.text: Analysis of 50 biallelic NOTCH3 cases demonstrated that biallelic LoF variants (n=26) display periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (n=24) show deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

hypotheses.text: Apparent anterior temporal lobe white matter abnormalities in patients with homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants represent generalized end-stage cerebral atrophy rather than the selective early anterior temporal pole T2/FLAIR subcortical hyperintensities pathognomonic of CADASIL.
hypotheses.rationale: Reports of temporal lobe involvement in advanced or adolescent homozygous LoF cases may reflect diffuse cerebral atrophy and confluent periventricular leukoencephalopathy extending into temporal white matter rather than isolated anterior temporal pole capsular lesions.

evidence.text: Stellingwerff et al. noted that vascular leukoencephalopathy from bi-allelic LoF variants is characterized by extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities and atrophy, while anterior temporal lobes remained spared early in disease.

new_directions.question_text: Does MRI longitudinal tracking in homozygous LoF NOTCH3 patients demonstrate secondary temporal white matter involvement with advancing age or disease duration?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether temporal lobe sparing is absolute throughout lifespan or lost as periventricular leukomalacia coalesces into diffuse white matter degeneration will definitively resolve conflicting radiological interpretations across pediatric and adolescent cases.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-cysteine missense variants in EGFr domains show an intermediate MRI pattern between classical temporal pole hyperintensity and periatrial volume loss?
new_directions.rationale: Determining how non-cysteine missense mutations differ from complete loss-of-function frameshift variants will refine the functional classification scheme beyond a simple binary dichotomy.
